simple.meaning: זֹהַר (zôhar) is a Hebrew word meaning “brilliancy.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: זֹהַר (H2096) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezekiel 8:2, with occurrences in Ezekiel, Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זֹהַר (H2096) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in זֹהַר (H2096) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: זֹהַר (zôhar) / H2096 is traced through Ezekiel 8:2, Daniel 12:3 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then I saw, and behold, a likeness as the appearance of fire; from the appearance of his waist and downward, fire; and from his waist and upward, as the appearance of brightness, as it were glowing metal.

timeline.evidenceText: Then I saw, and behold, a likeness as the appearance of fire; from the appearance of his waist and downward, fire; and from his waist and upward, as the appearance of brightness, as it were glowing metal.
Those who are wise will shine as the brightness of the expanse. Those who turn many to righteousness will shine as the stars forever and ever.

definitions.full: H2096. zohar זֹ֫הַר noun [masculine] shining, brightness (Arabic , Late Hebrew זְהוֺר , compare Aramaic זִיהֲרָא ); — absolute Ezek 8:2 ז ׳כְּמַרְאֵה like an appearance of shining (explained, v b, as resembling amber, חַשְׁמַל compare 1:27 ); also construct Dan 12:3 see foregoing.
